results.text:
# Dixon® Presharpened Golf Pencils, #2 Soft Lead, Yellow, Pack Of 144
Brand: Dixon
Category: Pencils > Wooden Lead Pencils

## Features
Quality #2 HB graphite core for smooth writing, ideal for standardized tests; Great for golfers, surveys, lotteries, compasses, etc.; Pre-sharpened to save you time; 3.5” length; PMA certified non-toxic

## Pricing & Reviews
Price: 12.79 USD.
Rated 4.7 from 1512 reviews.
Top review: I think these are great; I don’t have to waste a whole pencil on students who will usually not return them when finished. My students do not care for these due to the short stature and no eraser. Well, I’m short of stature, but full of knowledge to train them in skills, so don’t judge. It still fits their hands without the extended tail waving around that will end up in the parking lot or trash at the end of the day. Also, in high school, you don’t need an eraser in English. You need editing symbols. While I prefer pens, these work great and when they wander away and don’t come back, I still have plenty left and don’t feel sad about the cost. I just imagine that these little pencils end up assisting them in math.

## Details
Model: ‎14998

results.text:
# Pencils Pre-sharpened No. 2 144/box 12 Boxes of 12 New Improved Eraser
Brand: SEAGULL
Category: Pencils > Wooden Lead Pencils

## Features
NEW IMPROVED ERASER STRONGER THAN BEFORE; GREAT QUALITY PRE SHARPENED PENCILS; Pre-sharpened pencils for your convenience.; Non-toxic pencils.; Perfectfor school or office use

## Pricing & Reviews
Price: 13.75 USD.
Rated 4.6 from 823 reviews.
Top review: ExcelenteUsed for Operation Christmas Child boxes.I loved not having to sharpen pencils for my students that first time. When I went to sharpen them again (in an electric sharpener) some of the pencil lead was off center and were not useable. It could be my sharpener but I no longer mess with this and just throw them out. Out of 48 pencils, I probably threw three away. Hopefully it’s not a trend.I purchased this box of pencils for my daughters class. They are/was in need of supplies. The wood crafted very well, smooth with no loose pieces that can cause harm to the kids. The erasers are very moist and work well. I have gotten pencils in the past, not from here, but the erasers be really dry and wont erase and leave pink streaks on your paper. Also love that they are pre-sharpened.These pencils are great value for the price and I love that they come pre-sharpened. I bought these for my classroom and while they are convenient the first use, they are extremely difficult to sharpen. The wood breaks up completely by the sharpeners and the lead barely has a chance to get sharp before breaking out of the pencil. Many of these pencils only got 2 or 3 sharpens because so much of the pencil was eaten up trying to sharpen them. With that said, I clearly still find this value worth it because I have purchased this product twice. I think part of the problem may be the pencil sharpeners.Used them for Shoeboxes to be sent overseas. Like that they were already sharpened, and split into packages. I put one package to a shoebox and threw in a couple of pencil sharpeners.For a bulk pack of pre-sharpened pencils my expectations were fairly low, but the quaility of the product was surprisingly high, all the points were sharpened nicely, though the erasers are pretty cheap and fall out after mild use, the pencils also come with a fair amount of graphite residue on the edges of them. All in all, a great value for the size, but the erasers were pretty lame.We use these in our learning center, and the students use quite a few pencils per day. I ordered (4) boxes for a total of 144 pencils.PRO's:- InexpensiveCON's:- Lead breaks relatively easily- Although pre-sharpened, some still needed to be re-sharpened due to the wood shrouding some of the lead.- Lead not always concentric with wood requiring additional sharpening; otherwise, you can't write anything.- Erasers easily separate from the aluminum ferule holding them - only after a few uses.- Biggest issue was the gaps in lead within the pencils themselves when manufactured. For some reason, there are large gaps between when a length of lead ended and when it starts (within the pencil) so I end up sharpening a pencil a lot more just to reach where the lead starts again ... sometimes, I would have to go through an inch or two of pencil before the lead appeared. For a pencil that has a usable length of about 5-inches, wasting 2-inches in the sharpener is significant. This wasted much of the pencil, and I ended up throwing out many pencils because of the lead gaps and required sharpening which left me with stubby, useless pencils.Overall, I can't recommend these due to the amount of time I spent sharpening broken pencil tips, and of the lead gaps within the pencils themselves. See the pictures that depict the issues. I'll spend a little more next time and hopefully get better quality pencils.
